source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Recommend routine PSA screening for all adult men beginning at age eighteen","B":"Treat one elevated PSA result as diagnostic of prostate cancer without workup","C":"Discuss individual PSA screening benefits and harms with men aged 55 to 69","D":"Recommend routine PSA screening for all men aged seventy years and older"}}
source_row.rationale: The current final USPSTF recommendation (May 8, 2018; update in progress as of 2026-08-14) recommends individualized decision-making for PSA-based screening in men aged 55–69 after discussion of benefits and harms. It recommends against routine PSA-based screening in men aged 70 years or older.
source_row.source_detail: Final recommendation May 8, 2018: individualized PSA decision age 55–69; recommend against routine screening age ≥70; update in progress, accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: An asymptomatic 60-year-old man asks whether he should have PSA-based screening for prostate cancer. Which response best matches the current final USPSTF recommendation?
